### open-contracting/cardinal-rs
- URL: https://github.com/open-contracting/cardinal-rs
- Exact commit / revision: `7441f76529fbdefbc5666b4ce0d5b844e7f1056c`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Active MIT Rust engine that calculates procurement red flags and statistical indicators from OCDS compiled releases. The inspected implementation includes short submission period, single-bid, identical-price, late-winning-bid, disqualification, supplier-heterogeneity and heavily-discounted-bid indicators, with OCID/buyer/procuring-entity/tenderer grouping and configurable exclusions/statistical metadata.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It converts normalized procurement history into deterministic competition-friction evidence instead of another search surface.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon BD/capture, procurement-intelligence vendors, SLED consultants and procurement oversight teams.
- Painful problem: Historical feeds show publications/awards but not reviewable thin-competition, disqualification or pricing-pattern signals; rebuilding indicator semantics is domain-heavy.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price agency/SLED competition-friction diagnostic with every indicator linked to source releases, then recurring monitoring after source completeness is proven.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 2-4+ months of OCDS indicator semantics, grouping/statistical logic, configuration and fixture design.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact current revision; indicator source/fixtures/docs; `src/indicators/r018.rs` actually reads `tender.numberOfTenderers` and applies configured procurement-method filtering for single-bid detection.
- License / rights: MIT for code; upstream procurement data retains publisher terms.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT. Treat flags as review signals, never proof of fraud/illegality.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Modest attention and standards-tooling positioning hide a functioning procurement-risk engine.
- Value score: **28/30** — A4, B4, C5, D5, E5, F5.
- Combination opportunities: collectors -> immutable raw/hash -> `open-contracting/kingfisher-process` -> Cardinal -> CaptureBrief evidence packet.
- Next action: Run 2-3 rights-clean SLED/OCDS publishers and measure source traceability, missing-field behavior, indicator reproducibility and analyst review burden.

### miroslav-jokovic/fuel-guard — regulatory truth-release pipeline
- URL: https://github.com/miroslav-jokovic/fuel-guard
- Exact commit / revision: `768b541e0c5dd3171b1cbc57ef782384e09caa22`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong
- What it contains: MIT application whose undernoticed `hazmat-data` package implements an evidence-grade 49 CFR data release process using point-in-time eCFR XML, independent GovInfo CFR XML, frozen real-source parser fixtures, exhaustive cross-source diff/reconciliation, Federal Register/eCFR currency checks, SHA-256 release checksums and a provisional/fail-closed gate.
- Rare or undernoticed value: A regulatory dataset does not become production truth merely because parsing succeeds: unexplained source disagreements block release, effective-pending rules surface, attestation is part of the release path, and production clearing remains provisional until the gate passes.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon/compliance SaaS, eligibility engines, regulated logistics and audit products.
- Painful problem: Single-source regulatory ingestion can silently convert parser drift or publication lag into confident current-law conclusions.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Apply the release discipline to CaptureBrief FAR/DFARS/SBA reference releases with versioning, currentness checks, checksums and explicit provisional/unresolved states.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 2-4 months of source-triangulation, parser-fixture, diff, currency, attestation and fail-closed release design.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `packages/hazmat-data/RELEASING.md` documents eCFR versioner Source A, GovInfo Source B, frozen fixtures, exhaustive diff/reconciliation, Federal Register plus `latest_amended_on` currency checks, release SHA-256, named attestation and forced provisional state unless cross-check is clean.
- License / rights: MIT for code; government/reference artifacts retain source-specific provenance/rights.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT for software/pattern; independently establish rights/currentness for each source.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Zero-star app branding hides sophisticated regulated-data publication infrastructure in a subpackage.
- Value score: **27/30** — A4, B4, C5, D5, E5, F4.
- Combination opportunities: GSA FAR/eCFR/agency deviations/SBA -> parser fixture -> independent cross-check/correction review -> currency watcher -> checksum/attestation -> deterministic result only when verified.
- Next action: Prototype `verified/provisional/stale/conflict` FAR/SBA release states and prove stale/disagreeing sources cannot yield a definitive customer result.
